title: Experimental Design
subtopics: Design Limitations and Ethical Data Collection
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of experimental design and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply treatments and control groups in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Experimental Design is part of Probability, Statistical Inference, and Experiments. Start with treatments and control groups and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Statistical conclusions depend on data quality, design, assumptions and uncertainty, not just the value returned by one function.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Statistical conclusions depend on data quality, design, assumptions and uncertainty, not just the value returned by one function. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: State the question and assumptions, calculate a small example, and explain uncertainty or a limitation in context. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Experimental Design
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 148: Experimental Design
measurements <- c(3, 5, 7)
mean(measurements)

content_blocks.limitations: Treat this as a descriptive calculation; state the sample/design assumptions before making an inferential claim. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For experimental design, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

content.task: Apply experimental design to a small synthetic example. Start with treatments and control groups, predict the result, compare it with a local R run, test one edge or failure case, and document one limitation. For integrations or package-dependent topics, submit a safe verification plan rather than claiming the code ran.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the treatments and control groups idea in a minimal example or safe design sketch.
State the expected result before running the example.
Verify one relevant boundary, missing-value or failure case.
Record assumptions and one limitation of the result.
content.expected_output: A reproducible experimental design example or design sketch with the expected result, one checked edge or failure case, and a stated limitation.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
